akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي﴾: it is read with hamza and without hamza; [and] they are two dialectal variants. The hamza is dropped because this word is used so often.

akhfash:2-2.t: And He said ﴿فَذَلِكَ ٱلَّذِي يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ﴾: He means "he pushes him away from his right" (يدفعه عن حقه). You say "دَعَعْتُه" "أَدُعُّه" "دَعّاً".

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فَذلِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.
﴿يَدُعُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْيَتِيمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾ is negative. ﴿يَحُضُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلى طَعامِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمِسْكِينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ the fāʾ is causative (li-l-sababiyya); ﴿ويل﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of المصلين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿ساهُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the preceding الذين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُراؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the first object is omitted, its implied form being «الناس» (the people). ﴿الْماعُونَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "أرأيتك الذى"; the kāf is a ṣila (connective, i.e. a redundant addition) that may be present or absent, and the meaning is the same.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ﴾.
From دععت, and it is يُدعّ: he pushes him away from his right and wrongs him. Likewise: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَحُضُّ﴾.
I.e.: he does not attend to feeding the poor, nor does he enjoin it.

farraa:4-4.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾, meaning the hypocrites; ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلاَتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ﴾: he says: heedless (لاهون). Ibn ʿAbbās explained it so, and so I saw it in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd].

farraa:6-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ﴾.
If people see them, they pray; and if no one sees them, they abandon prayer. ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ ٱلْمَاعُونَ﴾: He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Ḥibbān narrated to me, with his chain of transmission; he said: "الماعون" is every kind of common kindness, even mentioning the bowl, the cooking pot and the axe.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said:] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, who said: "الماعون" is the zakāt.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, the like of it. He said: And I heard one of the Arabs say: «الماعون» is water; and he recited to me concerning it:
* يَمجُّ صَبيرهُ الماعُونَ صَبًا *
(Its white cloud-mass spews forth the water in a downpour.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: I do not remember its first half. «الصبير» is cloud.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Dīn
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أرَأيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ﴾ ("have you seen the one who denies the Judgement?"): it was also read ”أرَيْتَ“. The preferred [reading] is ”أرَأيْتَ“ with the second hamza retained, because the hamza is dropped only in the imperfect, in ”تَرى“, ”يَرى“ and ”أرى“, the original forms being ”تَرْأى“ and ”يَرْأى“. As for ”رَأيْتُ“, ”رَيْتُ“ is not soundly reported from the Arabs in it; but since the interrogative alif is at the beginning of the utterance, it made dropping the hamza easier. The preferred [course] is to retain it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿يَدُعُّ اليَتِيمَ﴾ ("repulses the orphan"): the meaning of ”يَدُعُّ“ in the language is "he pushes away"; and likewise His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 13] ("the Day they will be shoved into the Fire of Hell with a shove"), that is, they are pushed into it violently. So that is the one who pushes the orphan away from his right.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ المِسْكِينِ﴾ ("and does not urge the feeding of the poor"): that is, he does not feed the poor nor command that he be fed. It is also read: ”فَذَلِكَ الَّذِي يَدَعُ اليَتِيمَ“ ("that is the one who leaves the orphan"), whose interpretation is: that is the one who pays no heed to the orphan and leaves him neglected.

zajjaj:5-6.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ هم عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ هم يُراءُونَ﴾ ("who are heedless of their prayer, who make a show"): by this the hypocrites are meant, because they made a show of prayer only: when the believers saw them, they prayed with them, and when they did not see them, they did not pray. And it was said: "they are heedless of their prayer" [means] they delay it beyond its time; and whoever deliberately delays it beyond its time until the time of another [prayer] comes in, woe to him also, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ الماعُونَ﴾ ("and withhold small kindnesses"): that is, they withhold that in which there is benefit. ”اَلْماعُونُ“ in the Jāhiliyya was whatever has benefit in it, even the axe, the bucket, the cooking-pot and the fire-striker, and everything from which benefit is derived, little or much. Al-Aʿshā said:
بِأجْوَدَ مِنهُ بِماعُونِهِ ∗∗∗ إذا ما سَماؤُهم لَمْ تَغِمْ
(…[is not] more generous than he with his māʿūn when their sky gives no cloud [i.e. in drought].)
And ”اَلْماعُونُ“ in Islam: it was said that it is the zakāt and obedience. Al-Rāʿī said:
قَوْمِي عَلى الإسْلامِ لَمّا يَمْنَعُوا ∗∗∗ ماعُونَهم ويُضَيِّعُوا التَّهْلِيلا
(My people, upon Islam, have not withheld their māʿūn [zakāt] nor neglected the declaration of Allah's oneness.)
